title: Typed routes with Pydantic
summary: Register a FastAPI app, parse a Pydantic request body, and return a typed item.

scenario.briefing: The campus lab keeps its equipment list in a small Python service. The first endpoint must accept a typed request body and return the stored item with an id instead of echoing raw JSON.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: The app and both routes are already registered.
read_item receives item_id; use it to pick the matching record.
The stored records use one-based ids, so index with item_id - 1.
Build the response with Item(**item) after looking up the record.

misconceptions.diagnostic: Leaving the handler returning the stored dictionary without Item(**item).
misconceptions.feedback: The route promises an Item with an id. Construct the response model so missing or extra fields are handled explicitly.

misconceptions.description: Ignoring the path parameter and returning the first record.
misconceptions.testDescription: The GET handler uses its path parameter and returns a typed Item.
misconceptions.feedback: Each URL identifies a different record. Use item_id in the lookup.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a path parameter arrives as text.
misconceptions.diagnostic: Selecting the statement that an int path parameter reaches the handler as a string.
misconceptions.feedback: Annotate the parameter as int so FastAPI converts and validates it; invalid text returns 422.

sections.title: An app is a route table
sections.body: `FastAPI()` creates the application object. Each decorator such as `@app.get("/items/{item_id}")` registers a path and an HTTP method, and the `{item_id}` segment becomes the handler parameter with the same name.

sections.title: Pydantic models guard both directions
sections.body: A parameter annotated with a Pydantic model is read from the JSON body and validated before the handler runs. The return annotation tells FastAPI what shape to serialize; `Item(**item)` builds that shape from the stored record. Invalid input becomes a 422 response instead of a crash.

steps.title: Create a typed item route
steps.prompt: Edit main.py. Keep the FastAPI app and Pydantic models, add a GET /items/{item_id} route that returns the stored Item, and keep the POST route typed. Run the checks when done.

tests.description: The app and GET route are registered with FastAPI decorators.
The POST body is parsed by a Pydantic request model.
The GET handler uses its path parameter and returns a typed Item.
The app also exposes a typed POST route.

hints: Use item_id from the path instead of the first record.
The stored records use one-based ids, so index with item_id - 1.
Leave the POST route typed with ItemCreate.

steps.title: Routes and models

statements.label: FastAPI reads parameter and return annotations to parse requests and serialize responses.
A Pydantic model parameter is filled from the JSON request body.
An int path parameter reaches the handler as a string.
The decorator's HTTP method must match the verb the client sends.
A handler may omit all type annotations and still get request validation.

steps.explanation: FastAPI derives parsing and serialization from annotations. Path parameters are converted to their declared types, Pydantic models validate the body, and the return annotation describes the response.
hints: Check which statements describe FastAPI's annotation-driven parsing.
Path parameters are converted to the declared type.
Pydantic validates the body before the handler runs.
An untyped handler gets no request model validation.
